tasks.title: Fix test project infrastructure
tasks.description:
The test project has two blocking issues that must be resolved before any real tests can run.

**1. ProjectReference path bug:** In `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests.csproj`, the path `../src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.csproj` is wrong. From `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/`, `../` goes to `tests/` not the repo root. The correct path is `../../src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.csproj`.

**2. TFM mismatch:** Tests target `net8.0` but only the .NET 10 runtime is available on this machine (`dotnet test` aborts with 'framework not found'). Change the test project TFM to `net10.0`.

**3. Add Moq and System.Net.Http:** Add `<PackageReference Include="Moq" Version="4.20.72" />` and `<PackageReference Include="System.Net.Http" Version="4.3.4" />` (or use the built-in HttpClient from net10.0 — just Moq is sufficient) so HTTP handler mocking is available for later tasks.

**4. Add InternalsVisibleTo:** In the driver project, add `Properties/AssemblyInfo.cs` containing `[assembly: System.Runtime.CompilerServices.InternalsVisibleTo("LinqPad.Databricks.Tests")]` so internal constructors on HTTP clients can be called from tests.

**Acceptance:** `dotnet build LinqPad.Databricks.sln` with 0 errors and 0 warnings; `dotnet test LinqPad.Databricks.sln` runs and passes all current smoke tests.

tasks.title: Implement Databricks HTTP base client
tasks.description:
Create `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/Http/DatabricksHttpClient.cs` — a reusable HTTP client wrapping `HttpClient` for all Databricks REST calls.

**Responsibilities:**
- Constructor `DatabricksHttpClient(string workspaceUrl, string pat)` — validates URL (regex `^https://[a-zA-Z0-9\-\.]+(\.(azuredatabricks\.net|databricks\.azure\.cn))/?$`), stores PAT.
- Internal/test constructor `DatabricksHttpClient(string workspaceUrl, string pat, HttpMessageHandler handler)` for injection of mock handlers.
- `GetAsync<T>(string path, CancellationToken ct)` and `PostAsync<T>(string path, object body, CancellationToken ct)` helpers: set `Authorization: Bearer <pat>` header, serialize/deserialize JSON with `System.Text.Json` (`JsonSerializerOptions { PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true }`).
- On non-2xx response: read body, parse `{ "message": ... }` or `{ "error": ... }` field, throw a custom `DatabricksApiException(string message, string? errorCode, int statusCode)` that extends `Exception`.
- Expose `DatabricksApiException` as a public class in `Http/DatabricksApiException.cs`.

**JSON models needed now (add a `Models/` folder):**
- `PagedResponse<T>` with `Items: List<T>` and `NextPageToken: string?`.

**Acceptance:** Unit test with a `MockHttpMessageHandler` (manual `DelegatingHandler` subclass or Moq) can construct `DatabricksHttpClient` via the internal 3-arg constructor, perform a GET, and receive a deserialized object; also verify that a 4xx response throws `DatabricksApiException` with the parsed message.

tasks.title: Implement Unity Catalog REST client
tasks.description:
Create `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/Catalog/UnityCatalogClient.cs` using `DatabricksHttpClient`.

**Models** (in `Models/` or `Catalog/Models/`):
- `CatalogInfo { string Name; string? Comment; }`
- `SchemaInfo { string Name; string CatalogName; string? Comment; }`
- `TableInfo { string Name; string SchemaName; string CatalogName; string TableType; string? Comment; }` — `TableType` values include `MANAGED`, `EXTERNAL`, `VIEW`, `MATERIALIZED_VIEW`.

**Methods:**
- `ListCatalogsAsync(CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<CatalogInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/catalogs` with pagination (loop on `next_page_token`).
- `ListSchemasAsync(string catalogName, CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<SchemaInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/schemas?catalog_name={catalogName}` with pagination.
- `ListTablesAsync(string catalogName, string schemaName, CancellationToken ct)` → `IReadOnlyList<TableInfo>`: `GET /api/2.1/unity-catalog/tables?catalog_name={catalogName}&schema_name={schemaName}` with pagination.

Paginate by appending `&page_token={token}` and stopping when `next_page_token` is absent or empty.

**Acceptance:** Unit tests with mocked HTTP verify: (a) single-page response returns correct items; (b) multi-page response (two pages) returns combined list; (c) `DatabricksApiException` propagates from `GetAsync`.

tasks.title: Implement Statement Execution API client
tasks.description:
Create `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/Sql/StatementExecutionClient.cs` wrapping `DatabricksHttpClient`.

**Models** (in `Sql/Models/` or `Models/`):
- `StatementRequest { string WarehouseId; string Statement; string WaitTimeout = "30s"; string OnWaitTimeout = "CONTINUE"; string Disposition = "INLINE"; }`
- `StatementResponse { string StatementId; string Status; StatementResult? Result; StatementError? Error; }`
- `StatementStatus { string State; StatementError? Error; StatementResult? Result; }` (reused for poll response)
- `StatementResult { ResultSchema Schema; ResultData? DataArray; }` where `Schema` has `List<ColumnInfo> Columns` (`Name`, `TypeName`) and `DataArray` has `List<List<string?>> Data`.
- `StatementError { string Message; string? ErrorCode; }`

**Methods:**
- `ExecuteAsync(string warehouseId, string sql, CancellationToken ct)` → `System.Data.DataTable`:
  1. POST `/api/2.0/sql/statements` with `StatementRequest`.
  2. If state is `PENDING` or `RUNNING`, poll `GET /api/2.0/sql/statements/{statement_id}` every 500ms until `SUCCEEDED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, or `CLOSED` (use exponential backoff capped at 2s).
  3. On `FAILED`/`CANCELLED`/`CLOSED`, throw `DatabricksApiException` with the error message.
  4. On `SUCCEEDED`, build a `DataTable`: add columns from `result.schema.columns`, add rows from `result.data_array` (cast strings to appropriate .NET types based on `type_name` where straightforward; default to `string`).
  5. Support multi-chunk responses: if `result.next_chunk_index` is present, fetch `GET /api/2.0/sql/statements/{statement_id}/result/chunks/{chunk_index}` and append rows.

**Acceptance:** Unit tests with mocked HTTP: (a) immediate SUCCEEDED response returns correct `DataTable`; (b) PENDING then SUCCEEDED (two poll responses) returns same result; (c) FAILED response throws `DatabricksApiException`.

tasks.title: Implement connection dialog (ShowConnectionDialog)
tasks.description:
Override `ShowConnectionDialog` in `DatabricksDriver.cs` using a WPF dialog loaded at runtime via reflection to avoid compile-time WPF SDK dependency.

**Implementation approach (from memory.md):** Load XAML string with `System.Windows.Markup.XamlReader.Parse(xaml)` and find controls with `System.Windows.LogicalTreeHelper.FindLogicalNode(root, name)`. Call all WPF types through reflection so the driver assembly does not require the WPF SDK.

**Dialog fields:**
- `WorkspaceUrl` (text) — required, must match Azure Databricks URL pattern.
- `PersonalAccessToken` (PasswordBox or masked text) — required.
- `WarehouseId` (text) — required.
- `DefaultCatalog` (text) — optional.
- `DefaultSchema` (text) — optional.
- **Test Connection** button — creates `DatabricksHttpClient` + `UnityCatalogClient`, calls `ListCatalogsAsync`, shows success (count of catalogs) or error message inline.
- OK / Cancel buttons.

**Persistence via `IConnectionInfo.DriverData` (XElement):**
- Save `WorkspaceUrl`, `WarehouseId`, `DefaultCatalog`, `DefaultSchema` as plain child elements.
- Save PAT via `cxInfo.Encrypt(pat)` / `cxInfo.Decrypt(...)` — never store plain text.
- Return `true` on OK (committed), `false` on Cancel.

**`GetConnectionDescription`** should return `"{WorkspaceUrl} / {WarehouseId}"` (already partially implemented — extend it).

**Acceptance:** Dialog opens without crash on Windows/LINQPad; fields pre-populate from existing `DriverData` when editing; Test Connection shows green/red feedback; PAT is stored encrypted; Cancel does not mutate `DriverData`.

tasks.title: Implement Schema Explorer (GetSchemaAndBuildAssembly)
tasks.description:
Replace the stub `GetSchemaAndBuildAssembly` in `DatabricksDriver.cs` with a real implementation that (1) populates the LINQPad Schema Explorer tree and (2) emits a typed data context assembly.

**Schema Explorer tree:**
- Root: one `ExplorerItem` per catalog (kind=`Schema`, icon=`Schema`, `IsEnumerable=false`).
- Under each catalog: one `ExplorerItem` per schema (kind=`Schema`, icon=`Schema`).
- Under each schema: one `ExplorerItem` per table (kind=`QueryableObject`, icon=`Blank`) and per view (kind=`QueryableObject`, icon=`TableFunction`). Distinguish via `TableInfo.TableType` — treat `VIEW` and `MATERIALIZED_VIEW` as views.
- Populate children lazily only if LINQPad supports it; otherwise enumerate fully (the API is fast enough for typical workspaces).
- Respect `DefaultCatalog` / `DefaultSchema` connection settings to order/highlight default items first.

**Typed context compilation:**
- Generate C# source with a class `{typeName}` (default: `DatabricksContext`) in namespace `{nameSpace}` (default: `LinqPad.Databricks`).
- The context class should expose properties for each schema as nested objects, and each table/view as `IEnumerable<dynamic>` (or a typed row class). For initial implementation, dynamic is acceptable.
- Use `CompileSource(new CompilationInput { SourceCode = new[] { src }, FilePathsToReference = GetCoreFxReferenceAssemblies(), OutputPath = assemblyToBuild.CodeBase })` to emit the assembly. Reference the driver assembly itself so the context can call back into `StatementExecutionClient`.
- Set `nameSpace` and `typeName` ref params before returning.

**Acceptance:** In LINQPad, after adding a connection, the Schema Explorer shows the catalog/schema/table tree populated from a real (or mock) workspace. Build must succeed with 0 errors.

tasks.title: Implement ADO facade (IDbConnection/IDbCommand/IDataReader)
tasks.description:
Override `GetIDbConnection` in `DatabricksDriver` to return a custom `IDbConnection` implementation backed by the Statement Execution API, enabling LINQPad's SQL mode.

**Classes to create** (in `src/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver/Ado/`):
- `DatabricksConnection : DbConnection` — wraps `StatementExecutionClient`; `ConnectionString` encodes workspace URL + warehouse ID (PAT injected separately); `Open()`/`Close()` are no-ops (REST is stateless); `CreateDbCommand()` returns `DatabricksCommand`.
- `DatabricksCommand : DbCommand` — `CommandText` is the SQL string; `ExecuteDbDataReader(CommandBehavior behavior)` calls `StatementExecutionClient.ExecuteAsync(warehouseId, CommandText, ct)` and wraps the returned `DataTable` in a `DataTableReader`; `ExecuteNonQuery()` for DDL (execute, discard result); `ExecuteScalar()` returns first column of first row.
- Override `GetIDbConnection(IConnectionInfo cxInfo)` in `DatabricksDriver`: read `WorkspaceUrl`, decrypt PAT, read `WarehouseId` from `DriverData`; construct and return a `DatabricksConnection`.
- Override `GetProviderFactory` to return null (or a minimal factory) — `GetIDbConnection` makes it redundant per the LINQPad doc.

**Acceptance:** In LINQPad SQL mode, a simple `SELECT 1` runs and returns a result row. `DbConnection.State` transitions correctly. Exceptions from the API surface as meaningful error messages rather than NullReferenceExceptions.

tasks.title: Write unit tests with mocked HTTP
tasks.description:
Replace the smoke tests in `tests/LinqPad.Databricks.Tests/` with meaningful unit tests covering the HTTP clients.

**Test files to create or replace:**

`DatabricksHttpClientTests.cs`:
- Happy path GET returns deserialized object.
- Non-2xx response throws `DatabricksApiException` with parsed message.
- URL validation rejects bad patterns.

`UnityCatalogClientTests.cs`:
- `ListCatalogsAsync` with single-page response returns correct count and names.
- `ListCatalogsAsync` with two-page response (next_page_token on first page) returns combined list.
- `ListTablesAsync` correctly passes `catalog_name` and `schema_name` query parameters.
- A 403 from the API surfaces as `DatabricksApiException`.

`StatementExecutionClientTests.cs`:
- Immediate `SUCCEEDED` response builds a `DataTable` with correct column names and row data.
- `PENDING` then `SUCCEEDED` (two HTTP responses) eventually returns `DataTable`.
- `FAILED` response throws `DatabricksApiException` with error message from API.
- Multi-chunk response: first chunk + chunk-1 fetch are merged into single `DataTable`.

**Helper:** Create a `FakeHttpMessageHandler` in the test project that takes a queue of `(statusCode, json)` pairs and returns them in order. Use this instead of Moq for HTTP to keep tests readable.

**Acceptance:** `dotnet test LinqPad.Databricks.sln` reports all new tests passing (0 failures). No tests use `Thread.Sleep` — use immediate responses in mocks.

tasks.title: Add NuGet metadata and finalize packaging
tasks.description:
The publish scripts (`publish.sh`, `publish.ps1`) already exist and produce `.LPX6` and `.nupkg`. The csproj lacks the required NuGet metadata for the package to be valid.

**Add to `LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.csproj` `<PropertyGroup>`:**
```xml
<GeneratePackageOnBuild>false</GeneratePackageOnBuild>
<PackageId>LinqPad.Databricks.Driver</PackageId>
<Version>0.1.0</Version>
<Authors>hpractv</Authors>
<Description>Azure Databricks Data Context Driver for LINQPad 8+. Connects via Unity Catalog REST API and SQL Statement Execution API.</Description>
<PackageTags>linqpaddriver databricks azure unity-catalog</PackageTags>
<RepositoryUrl>https://github.com/hpractv/linqpad-databricks-connector</RepositoryUrl>
<PackageReadmeFile>README.md</PackageReadmeFile>
```
Also add `<None Include="../../README.md" Pack="true" PackagePath="/" />` to an `<ItemGroup>`.

**NuGet lib folder TFM:** Per the epic plan, the NuGet `lib/` folder should use `net8.0` (not `net8.0-windows`) for macOS compatibility. Add a `<PackageTfm>net8.0</PackageTfm>` override or use a `.nuspec` / Directory.Build.props trick if needed. The simplest approach: add `<NuspecFile>LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.nuspec</NuspecFile>` with explicit lib path.

**Validate:** Run `./publish.sh Release 0.1.0` (on Linux/macOS) and confirm `dist/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.0.1.0.LPX6` and `dist/LinqPad.Databricks.Driver.0.1.0.nupkg` are produced. Inspect the nupkg with `unzip -l` and confirm `linqpaddriver` is in the tags.
